info.description: API for configuring and invoking AI agents in epilot platform

tags.name: Customer Chat
tags.description: Org-scoped configuration for website and portal chat agents

tags.name: Agent Execution
tags.description: Execute AI agents and manage executions

tags.description: Manage knowledge sources used by custom agents

post.description: Creates a new custom agent. System skills cannot be created via this endpoint.

get.description:
Lists agents from both system skills and custom agents.
Use query parameters to filter by source, availability, or entity schema.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Filter by agent source (system = pre-built skills, custom = user-created)

parameters.name: entity_schema
parameters.description: Filter by allowed entity schema (e.g., "message" for email-related skills)

get.summary: Get the agent configuration by ID
get.description:
Retrieves an agent by ID. Supports both:
- System skill IDs (prefixed): "skill:email-categorizer"
- Custom agent IDs (UUID): "0336a235-9417-4dd8-894c-fe81285bba75"

put.summary: Update the agent configuration by ID
put.description: Updates a custom agent. System skills cannot be updated via this endpoint.

409.description: Agent changed during the update; retry the request

delete.summary: Delete the agent configuration by ID
delete.description: Deletes a custom agent. System skills cannot be deleted via this endpoint.

get.summary: Get the agent's identity for Flows runs
get.description:
The agent's own identity for runs started by Flows (internal auth): an autonomous Agent Auth agent at the
Access Token API, owned by the admin who activated it. `inactive` when none was activated; `expired` once
its lifetime (90 days) is over. Runs of an agent with an activation (behind the `agent-flows-identity`
organization flag) mint their tokens from it instead of using the platform service token, and fail with
`AGENT_IDENTITY_EXPIRED` when it has expired or was revoked.

put.summary: Activate the agent's identity for Flows runs
put.description:
Registers a new autonomous agent for this custom agent at the Access Token API (90 days) and stores the
activation on the agent. The caller must be a 360 user calling with their login token in their login
organization, allowed `token:create`; they become the agent's owner, and the agent acts with the owner's
current roles under `access_profile`. Activating again replaces (and revokes) the previous activation.
Available only while the PostHog flag `agent-flows-identity` is on for the organization; otherwise `403`
with `code: FEATURE_DISABLED` (`GET` and `DELETE` stay available).

400.description: Invalid request, or not a custom agent

403.description:
`code: FEATURE_DISABLED`: `agent-flows-identity` is off for the organization. Otherwise not a 360 user's
login token, another organization, or not allowed `token:create`.

409.description:
The agent's identity was activated or deactivated by someone else meanwhile; the agent registered by
this request was revoked. Reload the status and try again.

502.description: The Access Token API did not register the agent

delete.summary: Deactivate the agent's identity for Flows runs
delete.description:
Revokes the agent's autonomous agent at the Access Token API (with every token it issued) and removes the
activation. Needs `token:create`. Later Flows runs use the platform service token again.

204.description: Deactivated (or there was nothing to deactivate)

502.description: The Access Token API did not revoke the agent; the activation is kept

get.description: Returns the org's website agent (at most one) first, then its portal agents ordered by created_at ascending.

post.summary: Create a customer chat agent with default config
post.description: Mints agent_id (equal to runtime_agent_id) and compiles the runtime AgentRecord. An org can have at most one website agent (409 on a second one) and any number of portal agents.

409.description: The org already has a website agent

get.description:
Capabilities admins can enable and the places they are offered on.
Single source of truth for Agent Builder; capabilities that are no
longer offered are omitted, while already-enabled instances of them
keep working.

delete.summary: Remove a customer chat agent and its runtime projection
delete.description:
Deletes the place agent. For portal agents, also clears
`feature_settings.portal_copilot_agent_id` on linked portals (pass
`portal_id` when known, otherwise the API scans org portal configs)
before deleting, so a single request cannot leave an orphan agent.

put.summary: Replace the AgentConfig and compile the runtime AgentRecord

get.description:
Lists the conversations portal customers had with this agent, most recent first.
Requires `entity:view` on contacts. With `has_ticket=true` a page can hold fewer
than `limit` conversations; keep following `next_cursor`. `from` and `to` narrow the
list to conversations last active in that period; keep them unchanged while following
`next_cursor`.

parameters.name: has_ticket
parameters.description: Only conversations in which the agent created a ticket

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only conversations last active at or after this time

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Only conversations last active at or before this time

403.description: Not permitted to read customer conversations

get.summary: Get a portal agent conversation transcript
get.description: Customer and agent messages of one conversation, oldest first. Requires `entity:view` on contacts.

403.description: Not permitted to read customer conversations

post.description:
Executes an agent (system skill or custom agent).
Supports both:
- System skill IDs (prefixed): "skill:email-categorizer"
- Custom agent IDs (UUID): "0336a235-9417-4dd8-894c-fe81285bba75"

422.description: `mode: sync`: the input exceeds the model's context window (`error: INPUT_TOO_LONG`)

504.description: `mode: sync`: the model did not answer within the request timeout (`error: TIMEOUT`)

post.summary: Execute an agent with streaming response
post.description:
Executes an agent with real-time streaming of tokens and tool events.
Returns Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream with token-by-token output,
tool call progress, and completion status.

Unlike the async `/execute` endpoint which returns immediately with
an execution_id for polling, this endpoint streams all events in real-time.

Supports both:
- System skill IDs (prefixed): "skill:email-categorizer"
- Custom agent IDs (UUID): "0336a235-9417-4dd8-894c-fe81285bba75"

get.description:
Lists the executions of the caller's organization, optionally filtered by agent and status.
With a filter, a page can hold fewer than `limit` executions, or none, while more follow:
keep following `next_cursor` until it is null, with the same filters.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of executions to return. Values above 100 are capped at 100.

400.description: Cannot cancel execution (already completed or failed)

get.description: Returns the step-by-step reasoning and tool calls for ReAct mode executions. Returns empty iterations array for direct mode executions.
Returns the authenticated user's feedback for an execution.

put.description: Upserts thumbs up/down feedback and mirrors it to the execution's Langfuse trace.

post.description: Approves a pending tool action when execution is in waiting_approval status

403.description: The caller may not approve this execution (code APPROVER_NOT_ALLOWED). Only with the PostHog flag agents-strict-approvals on for the organization: then only the user who started it, or internal auth, can decide; an agent token never can.

409.description: The paused run cannot take this decision: code APPROVAL_EXPIRED when the approval wait already expired or was decided, code APPROVAL_NOT_SUPPORTED when the execution was paused by a streaming run, which cannot be resumed (cancel it instead).

post.description: Rejects a pending tool action when execution is in waiting_approval status

403.description: The caller may not reject this execution (code APPROVER_NOT_ALLOWED). Only with the PostHog flag agents-strict-approvals on for the organization: then only the user who started it, or internal auth, can decide; an agent token never can.

409.description: The paused run cannot take this decision: code APPROVAL_EXPIRED when the approval wait already expired or was decided, code APPROVAL_NOT_SUPPORTED when the execution was paused by a streaming run, which cannot be resumed (cancel it instead).

get.description: Reconnects to an execution's event stream after approval. Replays missed events from event log and continues streaming if execution is still running.

parameters.name: from_sequence
parameters.description: Resume from this event sequence number (for reconnection)

post.description: Initiates a streaming chat session with an AI agent. Supports server-side conversation memory via conversationId or client-provided history via clientHistory.

get.description: Lists conversations for the authenticated user, sorted by most recent.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of conversations to return

get.description: Retrieves a conversation and its message history.

parameters.name: message_limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of messages to return

delete.description: Deletes a conversation and all its messages.

post.summary: Submit feedback for an assistant turn
post.description: Records a thumbs up/down (with optional comment) for the assistant turn identified by its Langfuse trace id. The rating is persisted on the message and mirrored to Langfuse as a trace score.

post.summary: Upload a file for a session
post.description:
Registers a file the caller attaches to a message and returns a short-lived URL to `PUT` its bytes to,
with the headers to send. Attach it by its `fileId` in `createSession` or `sendSessionEvent` (`user.message`).
Only the listed media types, up to 10 MB.

201.description: The file, and where to upload its bytes

post.description:
Starts a session with an agent, optionally with the user's first message (`input`), which wakes the agent.
With a `requestId`, a retried request gets the session its first attempt created.

201.description: The session, and its events so far

get.description: The caller's own sessions, most recently updated first.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only sessions updated before this time (the last listed session's `updatedAt`)

get.description: One of the caller's sessions, with its current status. Another user's session is not found.

delete.description: Deletes the session and everything it keeps (events, files, workspace).

get.description:
The session's history as client events, in pages: while `hasMore`, ask again with `after` set to `lastSeq`.
Every event carries the `seq` it comes from, so history and live messages can overlap.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many stored events to read, at most 10000

200.description: A page of the session's events

post.description:
The user's input to the session: a message, an approval decision, answers to the agent's questions,
or an interrupt (stop the turn). Accepted inputs are handled asynchronously; follow the session's events.

502.description: The agent couldn't get access to make the approved change; nothing was decided, try again

get.summary: Get a link to a session file
get.description:
A short-lived link to a file of the session: one the user attached, or one the agent created.
Images open in the browser unless `download=1`; anything else is downloaded under its name.

post.description:
Runs a script in the caller's script session, without a model (the epilot MCP's `execute`). Its reads run
with the caller's token; the changes it records are not applied until `applyScriptRun`. Waits up to `waitMs`
for the result: `200` when it finished, `202` while it still runs (ask `getScriptRun`).

get.description: Where a script run stands, waiting up to `waitMs` (at most 20000) for it to finish: `200` when it finished, `202` while it runs.

parameters.name: waitMs
parameters.description: How long to wait for the run to finish, in milliseconds; at most 20000

post.description:
Applies the changes a finished script run recorded, after the caller's client confirmed them, with the
caller's token. Each request runs for a while; call again until `done`. Refused (`409`, nothing runs) when
the script failed, recorded nothing, or asks for something the caller's roles don't allow.
Logout. Every agent the caller's sessions act with ends now.

EpilotAuth.description: Authorization header with epilot OAuth2 bearer token. Supports RFC8725 for JWT validation.

IfMatchUpdatedAt.name: If-Match
IfMatchUpdatedAt.description: Compare-and-swap token. The agent's current `updated_at`; may be sent as `updated_at` in the body instead.

SessionsBadRequest.description: Invalid request: it doesn't match this spec (`issues` says where), or it can't be done as asked

SessionsNotEnabled.description: Refused (`code: not_enabled`): Luna is not enabled for the caller's organization

SessionsNotFound.description: Not found, or not the caller's

SessionsConflict.description: Conflicts with the session's state (e.g. an approval that expired, questions answered already)

SessionsPayloadTooLarge.description: The request body is larger than 256 KB

SessionsQuotaExceeded.description: Refused (`code: quota_exceeded`): the caller or the organization has as many sessions running as allowed, or the organization's daily budget is used up

retry-after.description: Seconds until it may work again

capabilities.description:
Configured capability instances, up to 30 per agent. The same
catalog `type` may appear more than once when `label` (name) or
`guidance` (when to use) differs between siblings.

instructions.description: Admin-editable briefing in the default `appearance.language`. Prefilled with a place default on create; omitted on save keeps the saved value.

instructionTranslations.description: Briefings for each language in `appearance.languages` other than `appearance.language`. Only present once the agent speaks a second language.

instructionsNeedsReview.description: Languages whose briefing changed in another language and are not checked yet.

starterKeys.description: One key per starter, in the order of `starters` and the same for a starter in every language; websites ask a starter by it with `startStarter(key)`. Absent for starters saved before keys, which readers key `starter-<position>`.

launcherLabel.description: Text on the Website Chat's epilot button, in the default language. Website place only; without it the Website Chat shows its own label.

language.description: Default language. The top-level texts are written in it.

followUps.description: Suggest follow-ups after a reply. Defaults to on for website agents, off for portal agents.

languages.description: Configured content languages for widget chrome (name, greeting, starters) and per-language instructions. Only present with two or more; always includes `language`.

translations.description: Texts for each language in `languages` other than `language`.

needsReview.description: Per language, texts that changed in another language and are not checked yet.

starterKeys.description: One key per starter, in the order of `starters` and the same for a starter in every language; websites ask a starter by it with `startStarter(key)`. Absent for starters saved before keys, which readers key `starter-<position>`.

AccessLevel.description:
Who may use a capability. `anonymous` = every visitor, `authenticated` =
only a customer authenticated by email code or portal login; others are
asked to sign in first. Each capability type has a default and a
minimum; values below the minimum are raised. Used today by
`open_journey`, `open_link` and `submit_meter_reading` (always
`authenticated`); other capability types ignore it.

SelfServiceIntent.description: What a journey, link or in-chat capability is for; names the action in the chat and in analytics.

ActionAutonomy.description:
Action capabilities only (`open_quick_actions`): per-capability autonomy.
`draft` = suggest only (proposal + deep link, nothing opens),
`approval` = the customer confirms in a card first,
`automatic` = run immediately. Defaults to `approval` when the
capability is enabled without one; unknown values become `approval`;
values above the capability's maximum are clamped down.

allowedDomains.description:
`search_web` only. Websites web search may use, normalized to
`host[/path]` (scheme, `www.`, query, fragment and trailing slash
removed; host lowercased; duplicates dropped). Empty or missing
allows any website. When set, only `web_search.search` is granted.

label.description: Admin label override. Kept on every capability so a disabled row stays listed.

guidance.description: Admin guidance. Kept on every capability so a disabled row stays listed; action capabilities also inject it into the prompt.

blockIds.description:
`open_quick_actions` only. Reserved tile allowlist (at most 200);
empty or missing allows every quick-action tile on the linked portal.

integrationId.description:
`view_hems_energy` only. Hub integration installation id used by
HEMS portal tools (`portal.hems.snapshot` via list_devices, and
when searchDeviceDocs is on also get_vendors /
get_connection_options). Chosen in Agent Builder via the
integration picker.

journeyId.description: `open_journey` only. The journey the Website Chat embeds; the action is offered only once set.

journeyName.description: `open_journey` only. The journey's name, kept for display.

url.description: `open_link` only. The page the Website Chat opens; the action is offered only once set.

searchDeviceDocs.description:
`view_hems_energy` only. When true or omitted, grants device
onboarding docs tools (`portal.hems.vendors` via get_vendors +
`portal.hems.onboarding_docs` via get_connection_options) once
an integrationId is set. Set false to disable. Portal place only.

instanceId.description:
Stable id for this instance within the agent. Generated when
omitted; send it back unchanged on later saves.

agent_id.description: Stable id of the customer chat agent; equal to runtime_agent_id.

portal_id.description:
Portal linked to this agent (`feature_settings.portal_copilot_agent_id`).
When set, only that portal is unlinked. When omitted for a portal agent,
org portal configs are scanned for matching links.

TicketPurpose.description:
Portal places only: purpose set on tickets the portal chat creates when
it hands over to the service team. Omit (or send `null`) for a plain ticket.

id.description: Purpose taxonomy classification id, stored in the ticket's `_purpose`.

name.description: The purpose's name, kept for display.

singleInstance.description:
An agent can have this capability at most once. Agents that already
have more instances keep them, but cannot add another.

requiresIntegration.description:
Only offer this capability when the organization has a matching
integration set up.

kind.description:
Where the website agent hands over when it cannot help.
- `phone`: the agent gives the customer the phone number in `value`.
- `email`: the agent gives the customer the email address in `value`.
- `journey`: the agent points the customer to the journey in `journeyId`.
- `ticket`: an authenticated visitor can confirm a support ticket for the
  service team, with the chat transcript as a note. Anonymous
  visitors are asked to sign in first.
- `unset`: nothing chosen yet; the agent offers no hand-over channel.

value.description: Phone number or email address for `phone` / `email`; empty otherwise.

journeyName.description: The journey's name, kept for display, for `journey`.

AgentId.description:
Agent identifier. Can be either:
- System skill ID (prefixed): "skill:email-categorizer", "skill:email-labeler"
- Custom agent UUID: "0336a235-9417-4dd8-894c-fe81285bba75"

KnowledgeSourceIds.description: Knowledge source IDs available to this agent. An empty array clears the selection.

AgentDomain.description: Business domain selected in the agent builder.

tools.description: Tool IDs this agent can use

availability.description: Where this agent/skill is available (flows, copilot, or both)

allowed_entity_schemas.description: Entity schemas this skill is allowed to work with (e.g., ["message"] for email skills)

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page. Null after the last page.

approved_action_ids.description: For batch approval - list of action IDs to approve. If not provided, all actions are approved.

rejected_action_ids.description: For batch approval - list of action IDs to reject. Actions not in approved_action_ids are implicitly rejected.

message.description: Free-text instruction or query for the agent

flow_context.description: Array of entities from the flow trigger context (e.g., the message entity when triggered by email receive)

attachment.description:
The file the agent should look at, referenced by S3 object. Only accepted by skills
that declare attachment support (currently direct-mode document skills). The object is
read by the execution Lambda and passed to the model as an image or document content
block; images must be JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP, documents PDF, DOCX, DOC, XLSX, XLS,
CSV, TXT, HTML or Markdown. Callers are expected to downscale images and cap document
pages before referencing them.

mime_type.description: Mime type of the object, decides whether it is sent as an image or a document block.

callback_url.description: Webhook URL for async completion notification

timeout_ms.description:
Deadline for the execution, counted from its creation. A direct skill still running when
it passes is cut off and the execution fails with `error: TIMEOUT`; a ReAct agent is cut off
at its next model call. Without it an execution is bounded only by the service's own limit.
Ignored by `mode: sync`, which has a fixed cutoff.

result.description:
Execution result (when status=completed). `GET /v1/executions/{execution_id}` always returns
the full result. The list endpoint and the completion event may instead carry
`{ result_ref, preview }` for a result too large to store inline.

structured_output.description: Parsed structured output (only for direct mode with output_schema)

stop_reason.description: Why the model stopped (`end_turn`, `max_tokens`, ...). Present for skills that run through the native InvokeModel path, so a caller can treat a truncated answer itself.

iterations.description: Slim, labels-only step-progress projection of the ReAct iterations (empty for direct mode). Exposes only index, tool, status, and timestamp — raw thought, action input, and observation are intentionally excluded.

tool.description: Tool id the iteration invoked, or null for a non-tool step

approval_note.description: Set when the usual approvers cannot decide this action. With agents-strict-approvals, a run started with internal auth and no user can only be approved or rejected by internal auth (the automation that started it); without its decision the approval expires and the run continues without the action.

AgentExecutionEventStatus.description:
Lifecycle status carried on an agent execution event.

Deliberately narrower than `ExecutionStatus`, which is the stored status of
the execution row: `pending` and `running` both surface as `started`, and
`cancelled` surfaces as `failed`. Consumers must not assume the two
vocabularies are interchangeable.

`queued` is non-terminal: the execution is waiting for executor capacity and will
be followed by `started`, and it can be published more than once if a throttled
execution is put back on the queue. Consumers must not treat it as an outcome.

AgentExecutionEvent.description:
Detail payload of the `agent-execution-status-update` event, published on
the AI Agents event bus with source `ai-agents`.

`execution_context` and `input` are present on every status, so a consumer
can tell whether an execution is theirs, and what it belonged to, from the
terminal event alone — without a secondary lookup.

executionId.description: The agent execution this event reports on

input.description: The execution input, as supplied by the caller of the execute endpoint

duration.description: Wall-clock duration in milliseconds, present on `completed`

message.description: Present on `approval_required` — what is awaiting approval

ToolPreview.description: Structured preview data for approval UI. Provides a generic format that any tool can populate.

summary.description: AI reasoning for why this action is recommended
summary.example: This email discusses solar panel installation and should be handled by the Service team.

url.description: Optional URL to view the entity

PreviewChange.description: A single field change in the preview

value.description: The actual value (type depends on "type" field)

description.description: Description for LLM to understand tool purpose

requires_approval.description: Whether this tool always requires human approval

AgentSource.description:
- system: Pre-built by epilot (system skills)
- custom: Created by organization

SkillAvailability.description:
Where the skill/agent is available:
- flows: Available in workflow automations
- copilot: Available as a sub-agent in copilot
- portals: Available in end-user self-service portals
- website: Website chat, explicitly selected; currently supports anonymous execution
- all: Available on the existing non-website surfaces; website requires explicit selection

ExecutionContext.description:
Where the execution was triggered from:
- flows: Triggered from workflow automation
- copilot: Triggered from copilot assistant
- api: Direct API call
- sharing: Triggered by sharing-api auto-sharing rules

ExecutionPattern.description:
- direct: Single LLM call, no tools
- react: Multi-step reasoning with tool use

ExecutionMode.description:
- automatic: Execute without human intervention
- approval: Pause for human approval before tool execution
- draft: Execute but mark output as draft for review

ParameterType.description:
Base types:
- text: Text input field
- textarea: Multi-line text input field
- number: Numeric input field
- boolean: Toggle switch
- select: Dropdown selection (requires enum array)

Custom types (domain-specific):
- entity-schema: Entity schema selector (fetches from Entity API)
- entity-attribute: Entity attribute selector (requires dependsOn)
- entity-id: Entity picker (search and select entities)
- taxonomy: Taxonomy selector (fetches from Taxonomy API)
- taxonomy-classification: Classification selector (requires dependsOn)
- shared-inbox: Shared inbox selector (fetches from Email Settings API)
- matching-criteria: Criteria editor for mapping compared fields between two contexts or entities

name.description: Unique identifier for the parameter (used in API)

dependsOn.description: Parent parameter this depends on (for entity-attribute, taxonomy-classification)

visibleWhen.description: Conditional visibility rules (show when parent has specific values)

schemaFilter.description: Filter to specific schemas (for entity-schema, entity-id)

attributeTypeFilter.description: Filter to specific attribute types (for entity-attribute)

hidden.description: Whether to hide the parameter from the UI

required.description: Array of parameter names that are required

thinking.description: Enable extended thinking/reasoning for the model

thinking_budget.description: Token budget for extended thinking (only used when thinking is enabled)

code.description: Machine-readable error code, where an operation documents one (e.g. `FEATURE_DISABLED`)

AgentAuthAccessProfile.description: Access profile of the agent's grant at the Access Token API (its ceiling)

reason.description: Purpose shown in the agent's token names and the admin view; required for any profile but `read`
reason.example: Labels inbound emails and updates their tickets

agent_auth_agent_id.description: The agent's id at the Access Token API

owner_user_id.description: The admin who activated it; the agent acts with their current roles

expires_at.description: End of the activation's lifetime (90 days); it is not renewed automatically

expiring_soon.description:
`active` and expiring within 14 days: an admin should activate the agent again, or its Flows runs fail
with `AGENT_IDENTITY_EXPIRED` once it has expired.

message.description: User message. Required unless `tool_approval` is set.

conversationId.description: Conversation ID for server-side memory. If provided, loads history from DynamoDB.

clientHistory.description:
Client-provided message history. A non-empty array overrides
server-side memory. Each item is a ChatMessage. Only the latest
100 messages are used; any other shape is rejected.

preview_demo.description:
Agent Builder place-agent preview: when true, portal tools return
synthetic demo fixtures instead of calling customer-portal-api,
and execution mode is forced to draft.

portal_config_override.description:
Agent Builder preview of a portal Customer Chat agent: the unsaved
place configuration (same shape as the customer chat config
update). It is validated and compiled like a save and used for
this request only; nothing is persisted. Requires preview_demo.
Not supported for Website Chat agents.

ToolApprovalAnswer.description:
The user's answer to an `approval_required` event (Luna behind the
`luna-tool-approvals` flag). Requires the asking turn's `conversationId` and `agentId`; `message` may
be omitted. On approve the server runs exactly the pending tool call
stored in the conversation, streams its `tool_call` / `tool_result`
and continues the turn. Errors: `APPROVAL_INVALID`,
`APPROVAL_EXPIRED`, `APPROVAL_USED`, `APPROVAL_UNAVAILABLE`.

reason.description: Optional reason, passed to the agent on decline

ToolApprovalRequest.description: A tool call waiting for the user's approval; the turn has ended.

input.description: The exact arguments that run on approve

AgentPreviewOverride.description:
Agent Builder preview: unsaved editor settings applied to the saved
custom agent for this request only. Nothing is persisted. Requires
preview_demo on /v1/chat and forces draft execution mode on
/v1/agents/{agent_id}/execute/stream. Not supported for system skills
or Website Chat agents.

mode.description: Stream mode - updates for step-based, messages for token-based

trace_id.description: Langfuse trace id for the turn (assistant messages only)
Langfuse trace id of the assistant turn being rated

contact_id.description: The customer's contact, known once the agent created a ticket

ticket_ids.description: Tickets the agent created in this conversation, oldest first

SessionsError.description: An error of the Sessions API

requestId.description: The request's id, for support (internal errors)

retryAfterSeconds.description: `quota_exceeded`: seconds until it may work again (also the `retry-after` header)

Refusal.description: A refusal the client tells the user about; `error` repeats it, like every other error

RequestId.description: The client's id for the request: sent again on a retry, it is taken once

SessionStatus.description: `starting`: its VM starts or the agent catches up; `failed`: its last turn couldn't run

SessionLiveInfo.description: How to subscribe to the session's live messages on AppSync Events

httpHost.description: Host of the Event API's HTTP endpoint (the `host` in the subscribe auth header)

realtimeUrl.description: WebSocket URL of the Event API

mode.description: `read`: the user signed in read-only (or anonymized), so the agent only reads in this session

lastSeq.description: The `seq` this page ends at; ask again `after` it while `hasMore`

MessageInput.description: The user's message, its text (trimmed), its files, or both

context.description: Where the user is (page, record); given to the agent, not shown as the user's words

ClientInput.description: The user's input to a session

UserMessageInput.description: A message. It closes open questions and expires pending approvals.

UserApprovalInput.description: Approves or rejects what the agent asked to do (`approval.required`)

UserAnswerInput.description: The user's answers to the agent's questions (`question.asked`), one per question

SessionInputAccepted.description: What was accepted: a message or an interrupt, an approval decision, or answers

name.description: Trimmed, and made safe as a file name

size.description: In bytes; the upload URL takes exactly this many

upload.description: `PUT` the file's bytes to `url` with `headers`, before the link expires

description.description: What the script does, for the user (trimmed)

waitMs.description: How long to wait for the result, in milliseconds

output.description: How the run ended: what the script printed, its result, its exit

changes.description: Changes the script recorded, not applied; `applyScriptRun` applies them

done.description: False while changes are left; call again

result.description: When done: what the batch did

data.description: Base64 data of a small image

SessionErrorCode.description: Why a turn or an input failed, for the user's copy

ContextBreakdown.description: What filled the model's context on one call, in tokens

BatchChange.description: A change the agent asks to make, exactly as it will run

title.description: The name of the record it changes

ChangeOutcome.description: What happened to one change of an approved batch

mayHaveRun.description: A failed change whose result was lost; it may have taken effect

header.description: A short label for the question

Answer.description: One answer per question, in order: the labels picked, and/or the user's own words

ClientEvent.description:
What a client sees of a session's history. Every event carries the `seq` of the stored event it comes
from, so history, live messages and reconnects can overlap and a client applies each event once.

ClientEventInput.description: The user's message, or their interrupt

ClientEventInputTaken.description: The agent took the user's message `inputEventId`, where it reads it

ClientEventInputCancelled.description: The message will not be answered: the user stopped the turn, or the session was deleted

ClientEventInputFailed.description: The message failed again and again and was skipped, so the session goes on

ClientEventModelUsage.description: One model call: what it read and wrote, and what filled its context

ClientEventContextCompacted.description: Older messages were summarized to make room; the context held `tokensBefore` until then

error.description: Details only; `errorCode` is for the user's copy

cutOff.description: The answer stopped at the model's output limit; the user can ask it to continue

reasoningMs.description: How long the model thought before it answered

marker.description: Why the runtime wrote the result instead of the tool

stepId.description: The read that loaded it; a client shows the skill instead of that step

ClientEventApprovalRequired.description: The agent asks to make changes: approve or reject with `user.approval`

changes.description: A batch: every change, exactly as it will run

executionId.description: The script that recorded the batch

ClientEventApprovalExecuted.description: An approved batch ran: every change ran, or it stopped at the first failure

ClientEventQuestionAsked.description: The agent asks the user: answer with `user.answer`

ClientEventFilesCreated.description: Files the agent wrote for the user in this turn

ClientEventQuestionAnswered.description: Answered, or `dismissed`: the user wrote a message instead
